notes: Lightweight linear probe on early transformer layers classifying and discarding noisy input chunks before the main forward pass; outperforms RAG baseline and LLM-Discrim on NoisyRetrieval/NaturalQA/TriviaQA
name: END (Early Noise Dropping)

title: Differential Transformer
notes: Foundational attention-mechanism modification (difference of two softmax maps) canceling attention noise/irrelevant-context overallocation; outperforms matched-size standard Transformer baselines at 3B scale
name: Differential Transformer (DIFF Transformer)

title: Activation-aware Probe-Query: Effective Key-Value Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs Inference
notes: Training-free activation-aware KV-cache selection improving long-context retrieval precision under sparse attention; outperforms Infinite/StreamingLLM/InfLLM baselines on Long-Bench, though primarily framed as inference-efficiency rather than pollution-defense
name: ActQKV (Activation-aware Probe-Query)

title: TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
notes: Compressor-Reader architecture reframing long-horizon agent safety detection as trajectory-level evidence compression, addressing sparse/delayed/compositional risk signals that per-turn guardrails (Llama Guard, ShieldGemma) miss; outperforms Base/SFT/AgentAuditor/MAGE on ASSEBench/Pre-Ex-Bench/R-Judge
name: TRACE (Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression)

title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding
notes: Agent-callable branch/return actions letting agents actively manage working context by folding completed sub-trajectories into summaries; RL-trained via FoldGRPO, outperforms ReAct and Summary Agent baselines at matched/smaller active context
name: Context-Folding (FoldGRPO)

title: Scaling LLM Multi-turn RL with End-to-end Summarization-based Context Management
notes: Periodic LLM-generated summarization of tool-use history integrated into multi-turn RL training to overcome context-length ceiling; outperforms vanilla multi-turn GRPO at matched/smaller working context on CodeGym and BrowseComp-Plus
name: SUPO (summarization-based context management for RL)

title: Curriculum Guided Massive Multi Agent System Solving For Robust Long Horizon Tasks
defense_name: UNNAMED: hierarchical pixel-agent grid with spatial curriculum and selective oracle
notes: Massively distributed multi-agent architecture (64x64 lightweight agent grid + Thompson-Sampling curriculum + selective LLM oracle) addressing catastrophic error compounding over long horizons; primarily framed as capability/cost-efficiency rather than explicit context-pollution defense
name: UNNAMED: hierarchical pixel-agent grid with spatial curriculum and selective oracle

title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: Trains a small external LLM manager to adaptively control context of a frozen, closed-source agent during long-horizon tasks; outperforms vanilla ReAct and SumAgent/other baselines on BrowseComp-Plus
name: AdaCoM (Adaptive Context Management)

title: AgentSwing: Adaptive Parallel Context Management Routing for Long-Horizon Web Agents
notes: Adaptive parallel context-management routing (vs single fixed strategy) for long-horizon web agents; outperforms no-CM baseline and static Discard-All/Keep-Last-N/Summary strategies
name: AgentSwing

title: Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems
notes: Runtime scheduling layer detecting trajectory instability via behavioral proxy signals and reallocating compute, addressing behavioral drift/coherence degradation in long-horizon agentic systems; improves trajectory quality vs peak-end and affect-only baselines
name: APEMO (Affect-aware Peak-End Modulation for Orchestration)

title: From Memory to Skills: Evidence-Grounded Co-Evolution Governance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Training-free framework crystallizing evidence-backed policies into executable skills to overcome passive-memory-retrieval limitations in long-horizon agents; best/tied-best on 5 EvoAgentBench domains vs EverOS/Memento/MemSkill/EvoSkill baselines
name: MSCE (Memory-Skill Co-Evolution)

title: Scoped Verification for Reliable Long-Horizon Agentic Context Evolution under Distribution Shift
notes: Graph-structured consolidation of a persistent system instruction to overcome flat-text maintenance failures over long evolution horizons; improves strict reliability (pass^3) from 0.091 to 0.673+/-0.136 vs HCE flat-text baseline
name: GRACE (Graph-Regularized Agentic Context Evolution)

title: CoCortex: A Memory Governance Framework for Reliable Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Memory governance framework grounded in Bayesian reliability theory treating memory as a first-class verifiable component to prevent silent error accumulation/hallucination persistence; fields largely empty in source data, limiting detail
name: CoCortex

title: Agent Delivery Engineering Predictive Reliability Framework
notes: Production monitoring/forecasting system aggregating 20 runtime signals into a Trust Margin metric to detect "false prosperity" (silent semantic-quality degradation) in long-horizon multi-agent systems; compared vs Kalman-filter-only baseline and traditional APM tooling
name: ADE-PRF (ADE Predictive Reliability Framework)

title: Trust-Aware Runtime Verification for Autonomous LLM Agent Systems
notes: Non-intrusive middleware computing multi-dimensional trust signals (action validity, memory consistency, communication coherence) to detect runtime trust violations from stochastic drift and error propagation; high precision/low false-positive rate, reduces cascading failures
name: TARV (Trust-Aware Runtime Verification)

title: STAR-PólyaMath: Multi-Agent Reasoning under Persistent Meta-Strategic Supervision
notes: Multi-agent framework (Reasoner/Verifier/Meta-Strategist with state-machine orchestration) targeting hallucination accumulation and memory fragmentation in long-horizon competition-math reasoning; best score on all 8 benchmarks vs frontier single-model baselines
name: STAR-PólyaMath

title: Is Deep Research Reliable? Misleading Knowledge Induces False Conclusions
defense_name: UNNAMED: pre-research and post-research verification defenses (verification-enhanced prompting + search-enabled verifier agent) for Deep Research agents
notes: Evaluates two mitigation strategies against constructed misleading documents (controlled institutional-authority cues) that propagate into false conclusions in Deep Research reports; ambiguous whether framing is adversarial-injection or naturally-encountered misinformation
name: UNNAMED: pre-research and post-research verification defenses (verification-enhanced prompting + search-enabled verifier agent) for Deep Research agents

title: HiAgent: Hierarchical Working Memory Management for Solving Long-Horizon Agent Tasks with Large Language Model
notes: Hierarchical working-memory management using subgoal-based chunking and LLM-based Observation Summarization to counter context redundancy degradation; roughly doubles success rate over STANDARD ReAct-style baseline
name: HiAgent

title: The Cognitive Bandwidth Bottleneck: Shifting Long-Horizon Agent from Planning with Actions to Planning with Schemas
notes: Alternative action-representation paradigm (abstract schema instantiation vs enumerable action lists) addressing the "cognitive bandwidth bottleneck" as environment action spaces scale combinatorially; outperforms planning-with-actions in large action spaces (SciWorld) though underperforms in small ones (ALFWorld)
name: Planning with Schemas (PwS)

title: OCR-Memory: Optical Context Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
notes: Represents long-horizon agent trajectories as images rather than compressed/summarized text to avoid the text-context-budget vs information-loss trade-off; outperforms Zero-Shot, Retrieval, MemoryBank, AWM, ACON baselines on Mind2Web/AppWorld
name: OCR-Memory (Optical Context Retrieval Memory)

title: When Child Inherits: Modeling and Exploiting Subagent Spawn in Multi-Agent Networks
notes: PDP/PEP-pattern capability-based access-control mechanism proposed to constrain subagent spawning/inheritance vulnerabilities (unrestricted memory inheritance, lateral compromise propagation); positioned qualitatively against prior model-level defenses, no head-to-head empirical baseline comparison reported
name: Agent Capability Registry

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
defense_name: DRIFT (Dynamic Rule-based Isolation Framework for Trustworthy agentic systems)
notes: System-level defense with Secure Planner + dynamic policy adaptation and memory-stream isolation addressing static-defense shortcomings of CaMeL; on AgentDojo reduces ASR from 30.7% to 1.4% (near CaMeL's 0.0%) with substantially higher utility; best security on ASB (4.8% ASR) vs 9 defense baselines
name: DRIFT (Dynamic Rule-based Isolation Framework for Trustworthy agentic systems)

title: Mobile-Agent-RAG: Driving Smart Multi-Agent Coordination with Contextual Knowledge Empowerment for Long-Horizon Mobile Automation
notes: Introduces named dual-level RAG technique explicitly targeting 'strategic hallucinations' and 'operational errors' from static internal-knowledge reliance; borderline whether this counts as a distinct citable defense vs. domain-applied RAG. No adversarial evaluation, purely capability/accuracy benchmarking.
name: Mobile-Agent-RAG (Manager-RAG / Operator-RAG dual-level retrieval augmentation)

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
notes: Clear named context-compression defense against context-induced reasoning distraction/context rot in long-horizon agents; evaluated purely against naturally accumulating context growth, no adversarial threat model.
name: ACON (Agent Context Optimization)

title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
defense_name: AgentFold (folding - granular condensation / deep consolidation context management)
notes: Named proactive context-management technique explicitly addressing context saturation (ReAct noise accumulation) vs. irreversible loss from naive summarization; evaluated purely on natural long-horizon context growth, no adversarial content.
name: AgentFold (folding - granular condensation / deep consolidation context management)

title: Memory as Action: Autonomous Context Curation for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
defense_name: MemAct (Memory-as-Action) with Dynamic Context Policy Optimization
notes: Named RL-learned working-memory pruning/editing policy explicitly targeting attention dilution/lost-in-the-middle from unmanaged growing context; evaluated only against natural context growth, no adversarial threat model.
name: MemAct (Memory-as-Action) with Dynamic Context Policy Optimization

title: SAM: State-Adaptive Memory for Long-Horizon Reasoning Agent
notes: Named memory-consolidation technique explicitly targeting inaccessibility of temporally distant info as context grows; extensively benchmarked against heuristic context-management baselines (truncation, recent-k, summary). No adversarial evaluation.
name: SAM (State-Adaptive Memory)

title: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
defense_name: ColorBrowserAgent (knowledge-aligned progressive summarization + human-in-the-loop knowledge adaptation)
notes: Named mechanism explicitly targeting 'long-horizon instability/decision drift' via memory-compression-based context stabilization, with ablation isolating the Summarizer's contribution; evaluated purely on natural degradation, no adversarial content.
name: ColorBrowserAgent (knowledge-aligned progressive summarization + human-in-the-loop knowledge adaptation)

title: Agent-BRACE: Decoupling Beliefs from Actions in Long-Horizon Tasks via Verbalized State Uncertainty
defense_name: Agent-BRACE (Agent Belief state Representation via Abstraction and Confidence Estimation)
notes: Named belief-state technique explicitly addressing context growing without bound and diluting task-relevant information; maintains near-constant context window vs. raw history/summary baselines. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Agent-BRACE (Agent Belief state Representation via Abstraction and Confidence Estimation)

title: HiMAP-Travel: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Planning for Long-Horizon Constrained Travel
defense_name: HiMAP-Travel (day-level context isolation + transactional monitor + bargaining protocol)
notes: Explicitly targets and directly measures mitigation of 'Constraint Drift under Long Tool Traces' (budget satisfaction degrading as tool traces accumulate); named mechanisms with dedicated ablation/failure-mode analysis. No adversarial evaluation.
name: HiMAP-Travel (day-level context isolation + transactional monitor + bargaining protocol)

title: HIPIF: Hierarchical Planning and Information Folding for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Learning
notes: Explicitly targets named failure mode 'long-context interference' (growing histories weakening global task-state tracking); trained end-to-end to fold completed subgoal histories, benchmarked directly against prior folding/subgoal approach HiAgent. No adversarial evaluation.
name: HIPIF (Hierarchical Planning and Information Folding)

title: ROMA: Recursive Open Meta-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
notes: Framework explicitly designed so 'aggregation compresses and validates intermediate results to control context growth,' addressing context-window limits degrading performance; however evaluation focuses on general accuracy/quality gains (SEAL-0, EQ-Bench) rather than directly demonstrating resilience to context degradation, so classification as a genuine context-pollution defense (vs. general architecture paper) is uncertain.
name: ROMA (Recursive Open Meta-Agents) with GEPA+

title: Prometheus: Towards Long-Horizon Codebase Navigation for Repository-Level Problem Solving
defense_name: Prometheus (memory-centric context engine with working memory over a repository knowledge graph)
notes: Explicitly targets the Needle-in-a-Haystack problem (relevant evidence overwhelmed by irrelevant code) via persistent working memory and knowledge-graph context engine, with dedicated ablation showing working-memory's accuracy and cost benefits. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Prometheus (memory-centric context engine with working memory over a repository knowledge graph)

title: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-guided Context Management
defense_name: AgentProg (program-guided context management with Execution Tree and global belief state)
notes: Named context-management technique explicitly addressing failure of existing compression methods to preserve vital semantic information; directly demonstrates avoidance of catastrophic degradation vs. sliding-window/summarization/hierarchical-planning baselines on long-horizon tasks. No adversarial evaluation.
name: AgentProg (program-guided context management with Execution Tree and global belief state)

title: ID-RAG: Identity Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Long-Horizon Persona Coherence in Generative Agents
notes: Named RAG-based identity-grounding technique explicitly targeting 'identity drift' as long-term memory context grows; directly measured mitigation of identity-recall decline over time vs. baseline generative agents. No adversarial evaluation.
name: ID-RAG (Identity Retrieval-Augmented Generation)

title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named end-to-end RL memory-consolidation framework explicitly addressing unbounded memory growth and degraded reasoning from full-context prompting; widely used as a baseline/comparison point in later papers in this batch (ReSum, Agent-BRACE, SAM). No adversarial evaluation.
name: MEM1

title: FoldAct: Efficient and Stable Context Folding for Long-Horizon Search Agents
notes: Named technique explicitly fixing training-stability failure modes (gradient dilution, self-conditioning collapse) in prior context-folding compression methods; evaluated purely against natural context growth, no adversarial threat model.
name: FoldAct

title: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
defense_name: CES (Coordinator-Executor-State Tracker), specifically the State Tracker context-compression module
notes: State Tracker component explicitly performs 'context compression and information management' to address lack of task-state awareness over long horizons, with ablation confirming its necessity; however core paper contribution is broader multi-agent RL-scheduler architecture, not primarily framed as a context-pollution defense, so inclusion is borderline.
name: CES (Coordinator-Executor-State Tracker), specifically the State Tracker context-compression module

title: Laser: Governing Long-Horizon Agentic Search via Structured Protocol and Context Register
notes: Paper's own threat_model explicitly names the failure mode 'context pollution' (noise from unstructured raw traces obscuring critical information); Laser's context register is a named mechanism directly evaluated for filtering noise and preserving essential state via ablation. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Laser (structured action protocol + context register)

title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
notes: Named plug-and-play context-summarization technique explicitly addressing context-window exhaustion in long-horizon web search agents; extensively benchmarked against ReAct, truncation, and MEM1. No adversarial evaluation.
name: ReSum / ReSum-GRPO

title: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research
defense_name: SearchSwarm (delegation-intelligence harness/training for main-agent-to-subagent task decomposition)
notes: Proposes an active delegation paradigm explicitly contrasted with passive context-management approaches (summarization/truncation) that wait until context budget is exhausted; core contribution is training data/harness for delegation skill rather than a pure architectural mechanism, so borderline as a citable context-pollution defense vs. a capability-training method.
name: SearchSwarm (delegation-intelligence harness/training for main-agent-to-subagent task decomposition)

title: Controlling Long-Horizon Behavior in Language Model Agents with Explicit State Dynamics
notes: Named external affective-state mechanism explicitly designed to fix 'instantaneous affective reversal' (abrupt persona/tone shifts) via temporal state persistence; unusual fit for the context-pollution defense taxonomy since it addresses persona/tone coherence rather than corrupted/degraded factual context, so inclusion is uncertain. No adversarial evaluation despite 'adversarial onset' language referring to a scripted hostile-dialogue phase, not an attacker.
name: Agent-level affective subsystem (VAD state dynamics)

title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Formal adversarial security paper: evaluates BOTH passive/incidental context-compaction decay of governance constraints AND an explicit adversarial Compaction-Eviction Attack (indirect prompt injection biasing the summarizer to drop a policy). Constraint Pinning is a named, ablated, training-free defense restoring 0% violation in both settings (though partially broken by an operator-impersonation rescind message).
name: Constraint Pinning

title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
notes: Named memory-architecture technique explicitly addressing failure of existing memory systems to capture causal/objective information and their reliance on lossy similarity-based retrieval; extensively benchmarked against many named memory-system baselines. No adversarial evaluation.
name: AMA-Agent (causality-graph construction + tool-augmented retrieval)

title: Memex(RL): Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Indexed Experience Memory
notes: Named indexed-memory technique explicitly addressing lossy information loss from truncation/summarization-based context compression, allowing exact evidence recovery via dereferenceable indices; RL-optimized read/write policy evaluated via before/after training comparison. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Memex / MemexRL (indexed experience memory)

title: Toward Ultra-Long-Horizon Agentic Science: Cognitive Accumulation for Machine Learning Engineering
notes: Named multi-tiered context-management technique explicitly reframing 'context saturation' (unbounded growth of execution logs/traces) as a cognitive-accumulation problem; ablation isolates each of the three HCC tiers' contribution. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Hierarchical Cognitive Caching (HCC), in ML-Master 2.0

title: MemWeaver: Weaving Hybrid Memories for Traceable Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning
defense_name: MemWeaver (graph memory + experience memory + passage memory)
notes: Named hybrid-memory framework explicitly targeting temporal conflicts, brittle multi-hop reasoning, and poor traceability from unstructured retrieval/coarse abstraction; ablations isolate each memory layer's contribution against named baselines (MemoryBank, A-Mem, ReadAgent). No adversarial evaluation.
name: MemWeaver (graph memory + experience memory + passage memory)

title: Beyond Compaction: Structured Context Eviction for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named, deterministic, LLM-free structured context-eviction scheme explicitly designed to avoid four stated limitations of summarization-based compaction (lossiness, causal-structure destruction, blocking cost, compression-induced hallucination); demonstrated across an 80M-token single session with no measurable accuracy degradation. No adversarial evaluation.
name: CWL (Context Window Lifecycle)

title: Beyond Entangled Planning: Task-Decoupled Planning for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named training-free framework explicitly targeting 'entangled contexts' where monolithic history causes local errors to propagate across sub-tasks; isolates reasoning/replanning to scoped sub-task contexts to prevent error propagation, evaluated against ReAct/CoT/Plan-and-Act. No adversarial evaluation.
name: TDP (Task-Decoupled Planning)

title: Memory-R2: Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
defense_name: Memory-R2 (LoGo-GRPO training) with shared-parameter fact extractor / memory manager
notes: Core novelty (LoGo-GRPO) is primarily an RL credit-assignment training algorithm rather than a context-management mechanism per se, but the resulting Memory-R2 system is a new SOTA memory-augmented agent directly extending and outperforming named prior memory-agent baselines (Memory-R1, MEM1, MemAgent, Mem0). No adversarial evaluation.
name: Memory-R2 (LoGo-GRPO training) with shared-parameter fact extractor / memory manager

title: MAGE: Safeguarding LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Threats via Shadow Memory
notes: Formal security/defense paper (shadow-memory guardrail) explicitly evaluated against indirect prompt injection and user-as-adversary tool-chaining attacks, including adaptive defense-aware attacks (PI2); compared against five named prior defenses (Spotlighting, Repeated-Prompt, PI-Detector, MELON, IPIGuard). Purely adversarial evaluation, no incidental/natural-degradation testing.
name: MAGE (Memory As Guardrail Enforcement)

title: M2: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
defense_name: M2 (Dynamic Trajectory Summarization + Insight Retrieval Augmentation)
notes: Named dual-memory technique explicitly targeting 'context explosion' and 'lost-in-the-middle' degradation in long-horizon web navigation; ablations isolate Internal vs. External memory contributions. No adversarial evaluation.
name: M2 (Dynamic Trajectory Summarization + Insight Retrieval Augmentation)

title: FS-Researcher: Test-Time Scaling for Long-Horizon Research Tasks with File-System-Based Agents
defense_name: FS-Researcher (file-system-based dual-agent: Context Builder + Report Writer)
notes: Named persistent-workspace/file-system architecture explicitly addressing context-window exhaustion in long-horizon deep research, with ablations isolating the workspace, dual-agent separation, and section-wise writing contributions. Paper's ethics section flags prompt-injection attack-surface risk but does not evaluate it; core method is evaluated only against natural context exhaustion.
name: FS-Researcher (file-system-based dual-agent: Context Builder + Report Writer)

title: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
defense_name: UI-Copilot (memory decoupling + Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization / TIPO)
notes: Named memory-decoupling technique explicitly targeting 'memory degradation, progress confusion, and math hallucination' in long-horizon GUI agents; ablates against context-management strategy variants (Action-Only, Action-Thought, Multi-turn Context). No adversarial evaluation.
name: UI-Copilot (memory decoupling + Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization / TIPO)

title: Meta-Cognitive Memory Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
defense_name: MMPO (Metacognitive Memory Policy Optimization) with Belief Entropy
notes: Named self-supervised proxy (Belief Entropy) and RL training technique explicitly targeting 'belief deviation' from recursive-summarization semantic noise accumulation; directly extends and outperforms RL-MemAgent using an identical memory workflow, isolating the contribution of the new supervision signal. No adversarial evaluation.
name: MMPO (Metacognitive Memory Policy Optimization) with Belief Entropy

title: Slipstream: Trajectory-Grounded Compaction Validation for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named technique explicitly addressing a structural validation gap in synchronous compaction that lets errors 'silently propagate' (paper explicitly cites 'context rot'); validates candidate summaries against the agent's continued reasoning using an independent judge signal. Evaluated purely against natural compaction failures, no adversarial threat model.
name: Slipstream (asynchronous, judge-validated trajectory-grounded compaction)

title: Goal-Autopilot: A Verifiable Anti-Fabrication Firewall for Unattended Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Formal, provable defense (No-False-Success theorem) against silently fabricated task-completion claims, framed by the paper itself as 'a self-inflicted, non-adversarial analog of context/state poisoning'; extensively evaluated against ReAct/Reflexion/StateFlow baselines including a controlled gate-ablation. Evaluated only against non-adversarial fabrication, not an external attacker, though the ethics statement flags adversarial-deployer misuse as an open concern.
name: Autopilot (gated finite-state-machine execution firewall)

title: Environment Maps: Structured Environmental Representations for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named persistent structured representation explicitly mitigating 'cascading errors' from raw session-bound context; ablated against both a session-bound baseline and raw-trajectory-access baseline to isolate the value of structuring evidence. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Environment Maps (Contexts/Actions/Workflows/Tacit Knowledge graph)

title: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
defense_name: StructAgent (unified causal state + verifier-backed state transitions)
notes: Named state-centered framework explicitly addressing raw growing interaction history becoming difficult to interpret/verify/recover, and self-reported 'DONE' claims lacking evidence-backed verification; extensively evaluated across multiple backbones and benchmarks against reproduced baselines. No adversarial evaluation.
name: StructAgent (unified causal state + verifier-backed state transitions)

title: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?
notes: Named hierarchical memory-centered coordination framework explicitly targeting 'context/state drift' across long-horizon multi-agent organizational simulation; evaluated against several general-purpose multi-agent baselines. No adversarial evaluation; borderline fit since primary domain is social/organizational simulation rather than typical agentic task execution.
name: TaskWeave (Formulate-Partition-Diagnose-Align cycle + dependency-aware trace memory)

title: Failure-Gated Hierarchical Memory: Preventing Memory Pollution in Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Critic-Guided Write Control
defense_name: FGHM (Failure-Gated Hierarchical Memory) with Failure Critic and LTM Pollution Rate (LPR) metric
notes: Title and abstract explicitly target 'memory pollution' (erroneous/outdated/over-generalized entries silently degrading performance); named Critic-guided write-gating defense reduces pollution rate from 38% to 9% per abstract's own reported numbers. Extraction fields (key_result/baselines/threat_model) were empty in source data so classification relies on the abstract alone, hence not high confidence. No adversarial evaluation described.
name: FGHM (Failure-Gated Hierarchical Memory) with Failure Critic and LTM Pollution Rate (LPR) metric

title: Beyond Semantic Organization: Memory as Execution State Management for Long-Horizon Agents
defense_name: MAGE (Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration) - hierarchical state tree with Grow/Compress/Maintain/Revise
notes: Named execution-state memory architecture explicitly addressing how semantic-similarity retrieval 'fragments decision trajectories and mixes valid and erroneous traces,' letting corrupted state contaminate the active execution path; ablations isolate each of the three maintenance operations. No adversarial evaluation. (Note: shares the acronym MAGE with an unrelated Track-A security paper in this batch, row 562 'Memory As Guardrail Enforcement' -- these are two distinct papers/techniques.)
name: MAGE (Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration) - hierarchical state tree with Grow/Compress/Maintain/Revise

title: PACEvolve: Enabling Long-Horizon Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution
defense_name: PACEvolve - Hierarchical Context Management (HCM) component specifically
notes: Paper explicitly coins and names 'Context Pollution' as one of three core failure modes (experiment history biasing future candidate generation) and proposes Hierarchical Context Management with pruning as the named mitigation, with dedicated ablation isolating HCM's contribution. No adversarial evaluation; failure mode explicitly framed as a non-adversarial analog of context poisoning.
name: PACEvolve - Hierarchical Context Management (HCM) component specifically

title: Memanto: Typed Semantic Memory with Information-Theoretic Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agents
defense_name: Memanto (typed semantic memory + automated conflict resolution + temporal versioning)
notes: Named memory-layer technique explicitly addressing 'memory poisoning' (accumulated contradictions from corrections/updated preferences/evolving context producing incoherent behavior) via automated conflict resolution and temporal versioning, alongside its primary 'Memory Tax' efficiency framing. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Memanto (typed semantic memory + automated conflict resolution + temporal versioning)

title: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
notes: Position paper proposing a named technique explicitly targeting 'context rot' and 'goal drift' from observation over-ingestion, but the paper itself states it is unimplemented/unevaluated ('whether SDO prevents the failures we describe in practice is a question that can only be answered by building and evaluating it') -- illustrated only via a hypothetical case-study walkthrough, not a real experiment.
name: SDO (Signal-Driven Observation)

title: ToolScope: An Agentic Framework for Vision-Guided and Long-Horizon Tool Use
defense_name: ToolScope (Perceive tool within Global Navigator / Agentic Executor / Response Synthesizer)
notes: Explicitly designed to 'mitigate visual context degradation in long-horizon VQA' via a dedicated Perceive tool maintaining situational visual awareness across iterative perception-action loops; evaluated against several baselines across four VQA benchmarks. No adversarial evaluation; borderline since the paper's broader framing (global planning + tool use) is a general capability contribution beyond just the visual-context-degradation fix.
name: ToolScope (Perceive tool within Global Navigator / Agentic Executor / Response Synthesizer)

title: ContextBudget: Budget-Aware Context Management for Long-Horizon Search Agents
notes: Named RL-trained technique explicitly formulating context management as a budget-constrained sequential decision problem, directly addressing both over-compression (erasing critical evidence) and under-compression (context overflow) failure modes; extensively benchmarked against ReAct, Search-R1, Summary Agent, and MEM1. No adversarial evaluation.
name: BACM / BACM-RL (Budget-Aware Context Management)

title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
notes: Named dual-granularity context-management technique explicitly addressing the KV-prompt-cache invalidation caused by naive text pruning/eviction; ablation isolates each of the two components' contribution against many named baselines (LLMLingua-2, SelectiveContext, Summary, MemOS, etc). No adversarial evaluation.
name: TokenPilot (Ingestion-Aware Compaction + Lifecycle-Aware Eviction)

title: Git Context Controller: Manage the Context of LLM-based Agents like Git
notes: Named version-control-inspired context-management framework (COMMIT/BRANCH/MERGE/CONTEXT) explicitly addressing unbounded interaction-history growth and lossy compression; extensively benchmarked with component-wise ablation against ReAct/SWE-Agent/Summary Agent/Folding Agent and 26 external systems. No adversarial evaluation.
name: GCC (Git-Context-Controller)

title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
notes: Named unified RL-trained memory-management framework (LTM+STM as agent tool-actions) explicitly addressing fragmented heuristic memory management causing context explosion and loss of rare-but-crucial details; benchmarked against LangMem, A-Mem, Mem0, Mem0g with ablations isolating RL and STM-tooling contributions. No adversarial evaluation.
name: AgeMem (Agentic Memory)

title: Addressable Recall Compaction for Long Context-Window Control in AI Agents
notes: Named ID-addressable archival technique explicitly addressing lossy compaction (discarding/summarizing/retrieving) that may remove task-critical details unrecoverably; benchmarked against Full_context, Sliding_window, LLM_summary, Structured_state, RAG_memory with statistical significance testing. No adversarial evaluation.
name: ARC (Addressable Recall Compaction)

title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
notes: Named context-management framework explicitly addressing the 'fidelity-tractability tradeoff' and citing 'context rot' as core motivation; keeps a complete structured log and uses coding-agent search rather than lossy summarization. Evaluated against multiple named harness baselines (WorldModeler, Arcgentica, Schema). No adversarial evaluation.
name: PRO-LONG (programmatic memory framework)

title: Self-GC: Self-Governing Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Named production-deployed context-lifecycle-management framework (indexed/recoverable context objects with a side-channel planner) explicitly addressing heuristic pruning policies being 'blind to future dependencies'; validated in live production A/B deployment and against multiple heuristic baselines. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Self-GC (Self-Governing Context)

title: LLM Agents Are Latent Context Managers: Eliciting Self-Managed Context via State Proprioception
defense_name: VISTA (Visible Internal State for Tool Agents)
notes: Named training-free interface explicitly addressing 'proprioceptive blindness' (models cannot see their own context's size/age/usage); extensively evaluated with ablations against many named baselines across four backbones and three benchmarks. Paper's own limitations section explicitly states it does not test 'poisoned external evidence' -- purely incidental evaluation.
name: VISTA (Visible Internal State for Tool Agents)

title: Unlocking Model Potentials Through Adaptive Multi-Agent Scaffolding for Efficient Issue Resolution
notes: Paper explicitly names and formally defines 'context poisoning' (test-overfitting and patch-overfitting from a single contaminated shared reasoning trace across localization/patching/validation) as its target failure mode; icat-agent's isolated-context event-based architecture is designed to structurally prevent this self-referential contamination, validated via a controlled communication-design ablation. Purely incidental/self-inflicted contamination, no external adversary.
name: icat-agent (decentralized event-based multi-agent scaffold)

title: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
notes: Named proactive context-management technique (context management as first-class policy actions) explicitly addressing 'prompt explosion' and 'dilution of critical cross-app facts' from passive ReAct-style accumulation; three-way component ablation and detailed hallucination-reduction error analysis. No adversarial evaluation.
name: MemGUI-Agent / ConAct (Context-as-Action)

title: TokenMizer: Graph-Structured Session Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Context Management
notes: Named open-source typed-graph context-management proxy explicitly addressing the structural flaw of flat-text truncation/summarization/retrieval discarding decision rationale and task status; evaluation is explicitly minimal (n=3 sessions, single weak baseline) and directional only, per the paper's own caveats, limiting confidence despite the clear novel named technique.
name: TokenMizer (typed knowledge-graph session memory)

title: EvoDS: Self-Evolving Autonomous Data Science Agent with Skill Learning and Context Management
defense_name: EvoDS - Adaptive Context Compression (ACC) component specifically
notes: Named component (ACC) treating context management as a learned control problem rather than passive truncation, explicitly eliminating out-of-token failures (0 samples exceed limits vs. multiple failures without it per Table 3 ablation); paired with a separate skill-acquisition mechanism (ASA) in the same paper. No adversarial evaluation.
name: EvoDS - Adaptive Context Compression (ACC) component specifically

title: Context-Agent: Dynamic Discourse Trees for Non-Linear Dialogue
notes: Named technique modeling dialogue history as a dynamic tree rather than flat sequence, explicitly addressing loss of coherence and inefficient context utilization from linear history treatment; ablations isolate tree structure vs. retrieval components. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Context-Agent (dynamic discourse tree)

title: A Scalable Benchmark for Repository-Oriented Long-Horizon Conversational Context Management
notes: Primarily a benchmark paper (LoCoEval), but also proposes and evaluates Mem0^R, a named extension of Mem0 integrating conversational and repository information into unified memory, which outperforms all baselines including sophisticated memory systems (MemGPT, LD-Agent, Mem0) that were shown to sometimes underperform a no-context baseline. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Mem0^R (unified conversational + repository memory)

title: Recursive Models for Long-Horizon Reasoning
defense_name: Recursive Models (recursive self-invocation with isolated subtask contexts)
notes: Named theoretical/architectural framework proving isolated-context recursive decomposition strictly surpasses single-sequence context management (e.g., summarization); explicitly discusses how discarding intermediate reasoning upon subtask return prevents errors from polluting sibling/parent computations ('directly relevant to context-poisoning containment via structural isolation' per the paper's own framing). Evaluated on SAT solving and Go against CoT/PENCIL baselines, no adversarial evaluation.
name: Recursive Models (recursive self-invocation with isolated subtask contexts)

title: Neural Paging: Learning Context Management Policies for Turing-Complete Agents
notes: Formalizes context management as a caching/paging problem with a proposed learned Page Controller and formal complexity/robustness bounds, but the empirical validation only tests classical caching heuristics (Belady, LRU, LFU, FIFO, Random) on synthetic Zipf paging traces -- the proposed Page Controller itself is not empirically evaluated on real LLM agent tasks in the extracted results, limiting confidence that this is a validated working defense versus a theoretical proposal.
name: Neural Paging / Page Controller

title: Yunque DeepResearch Technical Report
defense_name: Yunque DeepResearch - Dynamic Context Management module specifically
notes: Named module within a broader hierarchical framework, explicitly structuring completed sub-goals into semantic summaries to mitigate information overload/'escalating contextual noise'; ablation shows removing it causes the largest drops on browsing benchmarks. No adversarial evaluation; broader framework also includes non-context-related components (orchestration, supervisor).
name: Yunque DeepResearch - Dynamic Context Management module specifically

title: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
defense_name: Hybrid context management + deterministic programmatic safety checks / domain allowlisting / action restriction / least-privilege scoping (production browser-agent architecture)
notes: Formal, production-grounded prompt-injection threat model with proposed architectural countermeasures (code-level enforcement outside LLM reasoning, domain allowlisting, explicit confirmation for irreversible actions, least-privilege scoping) explicitly evaluated as superior to permission-based confirmation and classifier-based detection defenses; however, the paper's only quantitative results (85% WebGames success) measure general capability, not adversarial robustness of the security countermeasures themselves, and no coined single technique name is given -- it is a bundle of architectural principles rather than one citable method.
name: Hybrid context management + deterministic programmatic safety checks / domain allowlisting / action restriction / least-privilege scoping (production browser-agent architecture)

title: Adaptive Focus Memory for Language Models
notes: Named lightweight three-tier (Full/Compressed/Placeholder) context-management system explicitly addressing the 'illusion of memory' (textually-present-but-behaviorally-ignored constraints) under naive truncation/recency compression; ablation isolates each component's contribution on safety-critical and policy-critical constraint-preservation benchmarks. No adversarial evaluation.
name: AFM (Adaptive Focus Memory)

title: Parallel Context Compaction for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Serving
notes: Named technique explicitly addressing lossy, unpredictable (high run-to-run-variance) sequential summarization compaction that discards task-relevant information unpredictably; primary framing/evaluation is throughput/latency/predictability rather than information-preservation quality per se, though improved retained-context fraction is reported as a secondary benefit. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Parallel Compaction

title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: Named RL training strategy jointly optimizing task execution and summary generation, explicitly addressing information loss from naively unlearned/unoptimized compaction summarization; ablations isolate token-level loss normalization and cross-trajectory GAE contributions, deployed in production GLM training pipeline. No adversarial evaluation.
name: CompactionRL

title: Learning to Remember: End-to-End Training of Memory Agents for Long-Context Reasoning
notes: Named end-to-end RL framework with dual memory (core summary + structured CRUD Memory Bank) explicitly addressing passive processing causing 'context rot' and brittleness under frequently-updated long streams; directly extends and outperforms prior SOTA MemAlpha across 13 benchmarks. No adversarial evaluation.
name: UMA (Unified Memory Agent)

title: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
notes: Named task-agnostic memory technique explicitly framed as a mitigation for 'context-pollution/context-poisoning'-analogous degradation (paper's own words) from raw, verbose episodic memory diluting decision-relevant information; extensive ablations and information-density analysis across three heterogeneous benchmarks. No adversarial evaluation.
name: PlugMem (knowledge-centric memory graph)

title: MemoBrain: Executive Memory as an Agentic Brain for Reasoning
notes: Named dependency-aware executive memory technique explicitly addressing how unmanaged accumulation of reasoning traces disrupts logical continuity and task alignment; ablations isolate selective flush and sequential folding, compared against naive deletion/random dropping and named prior context-management systems (ReSum-GRPO, DeepAgent-RL, AgentFold). No adversarial evaluation.
name: MemoBrain

title: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction
defense_name: MGA (Memory-Driven GUI Agent) - Observer + Structured Memory
notes: Named minimalist framework explicitly addressing context overload and error cascades from raw sequential trajectory concatenation via task-agnostic observation and validated fact-based state-transition memory; component ablations show strong synergy. No adversarial evaluation.
name: MGA (Memory-Driven GUI Agent) - Observer + Structured Memory

title: Improving Coherence and Persistence in Agentic AI for System Optimization
notes: Named agentic-researcher architecture explicitly addressing the 'coherence ceiling' (context degradation/'context rot' over long single-context explorations) by decoupling exploration from a single context window via persistent structured knowledge distillation; ablations isolate Archive vs. Digest contributions. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Engram (Archive + Research Digest)

title: Fact-Augmented Lookahead Planning for LLM Agents
notes: Named fact-distillation mechanism explicitly aimed at reducing state aliasing from raw or insufficiently compressed interaction history; ablation (ReAct+FEC) isolates the fact-compression component's contribution separately from lookahead search. No adversarial evaluation; borderline since primary framing is planning-quality improvement rather than context-pollution defense per se.
name: LWM-Planner (Fact Extraction and Compression / FEC)

title: PRIMA: Operational Patterns for Resilient Multi-Agent Research with Verifiable Identity and Convergent Feedback
defense_name: PRIMA (context-boundary discipline + reference-material sandboxing + poisoned-output rejection)
notes: Explicit structural threat model targeting 'indirect prompt injection through inter-step context' with concrete named countermeasures (context-boundary discipline marking upstream content as non-directive, anti-SSRF/filesystem sandboxing for fetched material, a resilience layer that 'rejects poisoned outputs'); however, the paper explicitly states quantitative evaluation and baseline comparisons are left to future work -- only a qualitative case study is reported, so defense efficacy is architecturally claimed but not empirically validated.
name: PRIMA (context-boundary discipline + reference-material sandboxing + poisoned-output rejection)

title: MemFlow: Intent-Driven Memory Orchestration for Small Language Model Agents
defense_name: MemFlow (Router Agent + tiered Memory Agent + Validator Agent)
notes: Named training-free memory-orchestration framework explicitly addressing 'lost-in-the-middle' and context-explosion failures in small language models via intent-routed retrieval; component ablations isolate Retrieval Strategy, Router, Tools, Escalation/Validator, and Packer contributions. No adversarial evaluation.
name: MemFlow (Router Agent + tiered Memory Agent + Validator Agent)

title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs
defense_name: Taxonomy-Aware / Pipeline conflict-type-aware response generation (from the CONFLICTS benchmark)
notes: Primarily a benchmark/taxonomy paper (CONFLICTS), but also proposes and evaluates two knowledge-conflict-resolution strategies (Pipeline: predict-then-generate; Taxonomy-Aware: joint single-pass) that improve conflict-appropriate response quality by 5.5-9 points over vanilla RAG; a genuine but relatively simple prompting-based mitigation rather than a heavily engineered novel architecture. No adversarial evaluation -- conflicts studied are naturally occurring (temporal shifts, subjective disagreement, complementary answers).
name: Taxonomy-Aware / Pipeline conflict-type-aware response generation (from the CONFLICTS benchmark)

title: BordaRAG: Resolving Knowledge Conflict in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Borda Voting Process
notes: Named knowledge-conflict-resolution technique replacing majority-voting document selection with preference-based Borda Voting to handle diverse candidates and continuous relevance scores; abstract reports it outperforms all baselines on three open-domain QA datasets. Extraction fields (key_result/baselines/threat_model) were empty in source data, so confidence relies on the abstract alone.
name: BordaRAG (Borda Voting-based document selection)

title: Does RAG Know When Retrieval Is Wrong? Diagnosing Context Compliance under Knowledge Conflict
notes: Named inference-time diagnostic/mitigation technique for RAG knowledge conflict, evaluated primarily against deliberately constructed adversarial perturbations (worst-case TruthfulQA misconception injection, and an LLM-based perturbation engine generating Entity Swap/Temporal Shift/Logical Contradiction/Distractor Evidence attacks), with component ablations (Premise Isolation, Divergence Check) and a length-matched sham-prompt control ruling out confounds. Paper explicitly notes real-world organic adversarial retrieval pipelines are out of scope, but the evaluated perturbations are crafted/adversarial rather than naturally occurring.
name: CDD (Context-Driven Decomposition)

title: SHIFT: Gate-Modulated Activation Steering for Knowledge Conflict Mitigation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Named lightweight learnable-gate technique for knowledge-conflict resolution in RAG, replacing brittle neuron-level editing; extensive ablations and cross-model generalization tests, including an explicit counterfactual/misleading-context case study. No external adversary, but directly tests resistance to misleading injected context.
name: SHIFT (gate-modulated activation steering)

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Named plug-and-play knowledge-conflict-resolution technique (dual contrastive encoders + self-answerability + SNR-weighted soft-prompt); benchmarked against Astute RAG, IRCAN, RAAT and others, with robustness tested under 30% distractor-noise injection. No external adversary.
name: TCR (Transparent Conflict Resolution)

title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Named knowledge-conflict-resolution framework explicitly diagnosing/reconciling parametric-vs-retrieved discrepancies at the fact level rather than suppressing parametric knowledge; extensive ablations isolate Self-Think module contribution. No adversarial evaluation.
name: FaithfulRAG (fact-level conflict modeling + Self-Think)

title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Vision Language Models via Knowledge Conflict Mitigation
notes: Named training-free plug-and-play technique for multimodal RAG knowledge-conflict mitigation via attention reweighting, neuron pruning, and context-logit amplification; abstract states it outperforms SOTA by large margins. Extraction fields (key_result/baselines/threat_model) were empty in source data, limiting confidence.
name: KCM (Knowledge Conflict Mitigation)

title: Micro-Act: Mitigating Knowledge Conflict in LLM-based RAG via Actionable Self-Reasoning
notes: Named technique explicitly addressing 'over-rationalization' where LLMs treat conflicting evidence as simultaneously valid; adaptively decomposes knowledge sources into fine-grained comparisons rather than superficial side-by-side comparison. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Micro-Act (hierarchical action-space decomposition)

title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conflict-Driven Summarization
defense_name: CARE-RAG (Conflict-Aware and Reliable Evidence for RAG)
notes: Named three-stage conflict-driven-summarization framework (parameter-aware evidence, context-aware evidence refinement, distilled conflict-driven summarizer); ablations isolate each stage's contribution, largest from retrieved-evidence refinement. Paper briefly notes relevance to 'adversarial or noisy retrieval settings' but evaluation itself is non-adversarial.
name: CARE-RAG (Conflict-Aware and Reliable Evidence for RAG)

title: TruthfulRAG: Resolving Factual-level Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs
notes: Named first-of-kind knowledge-graph-based factual-level conflict resolution technique (entropy-based filtering to locate conflicting elements); outperforms FaithfulRAG, COIECD, KRE across datasets/backbones with component ablations. No adversarial evaluation.
name: TruthfulRAG (knowledge-graph-based factual conflict resolution)

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
notes: Named mechanistic-interpretability-based technique that prunes conflicting 'memory heads' vs. 'context heads' attention heads to flexibly control internal-memory vs. external-context reliance; demonstrates cross-model/cross-relation/cross-format generalization against Prompt/CAD/Gradient baselines. No adversarial evaluation.
name: PH3 (Pruning Head via PatH PatcHing)

title: Dynamic Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation for Test-time Knowledge Enhancement
notes: Named technique using a lightweight parameter translator to convert documents into parametric knowledge at test time, explicitly resolving knowledge conflicts in a plug-and-play manner; directly extends and reduces cost versus prior PRAG method. No adversarial evaluation.
name: DyPRAG (Dynamic Parametric RAG)

title: Tug-of-War within A Decade: Conflict Resolution in Vulnerability Analysis via Teacher-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generations
defense_name: CRVA-TGRAG (Conflict Resolution in Vulnerability Analysis via Teacher-Guided RAG)
notes: Named two-stage domain-specific (CVE/vulnerability analysis) framework combining optimized retrieval with teacher-guided DPO fine-tuning to mitigate knowledge staleness/conflict; ablation isolates RAG-only vs. DPO-only contributions. Non-adversarial despite cybersecurity-adjacent domain.
name: CRVA-TGRAG (Conflict Resolution in Vulnerability Analysis via Teacher-Guided RAG)

title: Conflict-Aware RAG: Multi-Stage Learning with Conflict Signals for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Named multi-stage training framework with a conflict-quantification signal (ConScore) guiding SFT, DPO, and reranking; abstract claims significant outperformance of mainstream baselines across six QA datasets. Extraction fields (key_result/baselines/threat_model) were empty in source data, limiting confidence.
name: Conflict-Aware RAG (ConScore signal + multi-stage SFT/DPO/reranking)

title: Navigating Unreliable Parametric and Contextual Knowledge: Explicit Knowledge Conflict Resolution for LLM Inference
notes: Named multi-agent knowledge-conflict-resolution framework moving beyond binary source-privileging, using semantic-entropy-based confidence estimation and rule-induction/conflict-analysis/resolution agents; stress-tested under increasing distractor-paragraph noise ratios (up to 75%), showing much more graceful degradation than baselines. No external adversary.
name: MACR (multi-agent conflict resolution)

title: ConflictRAG: Detecting and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval Augmented Generation
defense_name: ConflictRAG (two-stage detection + Entropy-TOPSIS credibility + CARS metric)
notes: Named conflict-aware RAG framework with three components (detection, source-credibility ranking, diagnostic CARS score); benchmarked against Standard RAG, RAG+Reranking, Self-RAG, CRAG, NLI-Filter, CoT Detection with per-module ablations. No adversarial evaluation (naturally occurring inter-document conflicts).
name: ConflictRAG (two-stage detection + Entropy-TOPSIS credibility + CARS metric)

title: Tug-of-War between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
notes: Named contrastive-decoding technique explicitly calibrating model confidence to resolve both memory-vs-external and truthful-vs-misleading knowledge conflicts; extensive behavioral analysis of RALM biases (Dunning-Kruger effect, availability bias, majority rule, confirmation bias) motivates the method. Counterfactual evidence used in evaluation is synthetically constructed for controlled testing, not framed as an adversarial attack.
name: CD2 (Conflict-Disentangle Contrastive Decoding)

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
defense_name: ParamMute (Parametric Knowledge Muting through FFN Suppression)
notes: Named mechanistic technique identifying and suppressing unfaithfulness-associated FFN layers to reduce parametric-memory reliance; introduces a new benchmark (CoFaithfulQA) and includes causal validation experiment. No adversarial evaluation.
name: ParamMute (Parametric Knowledge Muting through FFN Suppression)

title: Accommodate Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-augmented LLMs: Towards Robust Response Generation in the Wild
notes: Named information-theoretic technique grounded in a novel analysis of when LLMs confidently resolve vs. experience uncertainty under knowledge conflict; integrated into and improves Naive RAG, Self-RAG, and Astute RAG. No adversarial evaluation.
name: Swin-VIB (variational information bottleneck pipeline)

title: Eliminating Retrieval Knowledge Conflicts: Cross-Validation Re-ranking with Large Language Models
notes: Named re-ranking technique explicitly targeting inter-context knowledge conflicts during retrieval (prioritizing reliability over pure relevance); introduces new ContraPRT benchmark. Extraction fields (key_result/baselines/threat_model) were empty in source data, limiting confidence.
name: Cross-Validation Re-ranking (inter-context conflict-aware re-ranking)

title: KnowPO: Knowledge-aware Preference Optimization for Controllable Knowledge Selection in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
notes: Named preference-optimization technique explicitly targeting 'contextual ignorance' and 'contextual overinclusion' via a general knowledge-conflict-dataset construction paradigm and DPO training; extensive ablations (SFT/DPO phases, data-length alignment, preference-ratio balancing) and OOD generalization tests. No adversarial evaluation, though paper explicitly notes relevance to adversarially poisoned context as a related concern.
name: KnowPO (Knowledge-aware Preference Optimization)

title: RPO: Retrieval Preference Optimization for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Named lightweight alignment technique integrating retrieval-relevance evaluation into the reward model in a single inference call (vs. 2-11 for Self-RAG/CRAG); robustness explicitly tested under deliberately low-quality (all-incorrect) retrieval. No adversarial evaluation.
name: RPO (Retrieval Preference Optimization)

title: Beyond Black-Box Interventions: Latent Probing for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
defense_name: ProbeRAG (knowledge pruning + latent conflict probing + conflict-aware attention)
notes: Named three-stage technique operating on internal latent representations (linearly separable conflicting/aligned knowledge states) rather than black-box prompting/decoding; extensively benchmarked against FaithfulRAG, CANOE, ParamMute, CAD, COIECD, AdaCAD with per-module ablations. No adversarial evaluation.
name: ProbeRAG (knowledge pruning + latent conflict probing + conflict-aware attention)

title: Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra for Taint Confinement in LLM Agents
notes: Formal information-flow-control (IFC) security framework with a fully stated threat model (policy-untrusted LLM, indirect prompt injection or hallucinated reasoning); proven security guarantees (parent label preservation, merge confinement) and empirically evaluated on a multi-turn tool-chaining exfiltration benchmark, reducing attack success rate from 31-50% to 0-7% across four models, with causal ablation isolating the branching mechanism's utility contribution. Compared directly against Microsoft Agent Framework's Fides IFC system.
name: APPA (Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra)

title: Data Leakage Prevention in Agentic Applications via Preemptive Hardening
notes: Formal threat model targeting data leakage via prompt injection/instruction-data boundary failures; pre-deployment pipeline evaluated on five real-world agentic applications and AgentDojo, achieving 100% ASR reduction under basic attacks and 91% under stress-induced manipulation, with module-wise ablation and comparison against FIDES.
name: UNNAMED: Pre-deployment scan/harden/validate pipeline (Analyzer/Modifier/Validator)

title: Twin Agent: Context Residual Compression for Privilege Separated Agents
defense_name: Twin Agent (Explore Agent / Safe Agent residual-hint privilege separation)
notes: Named privilege-separation design pattern evaluated on SWE-bench Lite, AgentDojo, and DecodingTrust-Agent against undefended agents and CaMeL; near-zero ASR while preserving utility, further stress-tested with an adaptive PAIR-optimized two-phase attack showing partial but not complete compromise.
name: Twin Agent (Explore Agent / Safe Agent residual-hint privilege separation)

title: PromptSentinel-X: A Leakage-Aware and Context-Aware Framework for Prompt-Injection Detection in Large Language Model-Powered Web Agents
notes: Named leakage-aware, context-aware prompt-injection screening framework with detailed reported metrics (0.9849 accuracy, 0.9851 attack recall) in the abstract, though key_result/baselines/threat_model extraction fields were empty in source data, limiting confidence in the full evaluation methodology.
name: PromptSentinel-X

title: Context Contamination in LLM Analysis of Network Security Logs: Poison with Passive Prompt Injection and Mitigation Evaluation
defense_name: UNNAMED: Layered defense (input filtering + prompt hardening/spotlighting + output validation) against passive prompt injection
notes: Primarily introduces a novel attack (LogInject / passive prompt injection / Context Stitching), but also systematically evaluates a layered combination of defenses (rather than one single novel named technique) achieving 90.4% attack-success reduction with 8.4% residual vulnerability and a documented utility cost; the defense contribution is a specific evaluated combination/methodology rather than a single coined technique.
name: UNNAMED: Layered defense (input filtering + prompt hardening/spotlighting + output validation) against passive prompt injection

title: Context-to-Execution Integrity for LLM Agents
notes: Formal execution-boundary/authority-binding defense system with explicit threat model ('authority laundering'); evaluated across AgentDojo live episodes, a code-agent benchmark, and hosted/API traces, recording zero observed field/effect/invocation escapes despite substantial adversarial proposal pressure.
name: CXI (Context-to-Execution Integrity)

title: aiAuthZ: Off-Host, Identity-Bound Authorization for AI Agents
notes: Named off-host authorization gateway with formal threat model, evaluated across 15 LLMs and eight real-incident-derived attack scenarios plus the AgentDojo banking suite; reduces residual attack success to 0% for all models, compared against content-safety classifiers, spotlighting, and reduced-policy ablations.
name: aiAuthZ (identity-bound off-host authorization gateway)

title: Agent Security Meets Regulatory Reality -- A Practitioner Systematization of Autonomous-Agent Threats and Controls in Regulated Financial Systems
defense_name: Pattern D: Inference-boundary redaction proxy (PII extraction/tokenization before model inference)
notes: Practitioner case-study paper documenting four production architectural patterns for a regulated KYC deployment; Pattern D specifically narrows the prompt-injection surface by redacting/tokenizing PII before inference, but the paper reports production audit findings and negative results rather than a controlled red-team/ASR evaluation, so defense efficacy is documented but not rigorously benchmarked.
name: Pattern D: Inference-boundary redaction proxy (PII extraction/tokenization before model inference)

title: Verifying Intent and Harm: A Unified Defense Against LLM-Generated Threats
defense_name: Prompt-response verification framework (Task Analyst + Safety Analyst + Judge)
notes: Named joint prompt-intent/response-harm verification defense with formalized 'prompt-response attack' / intent-harm-separation threat model; evaluated across five threat categories against single-sided baselines (PromptGuard-2, InjecGuard, LlamaGuard, etc.) and architecture-aware adaptive attacks with detailed ablations.
name: Prompt-response verification framework (Task Analyst + Safety Analyst + Judge)

title: GIF: Locally Sound Geometric Information Flow Control for LLMs
notes: Named IFC defense with a mechanized formal soundness proof (Lean 4), targeting both integrity (prompt injection) and confidentiality (leakage) attacks; evaluated against attention-based (RTBAS) and LLM-as-judge baselines across multiple benchmarks, including transfer from small surrogate models.
name: GIF (Geometric Information Flow)

title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents
notes: Named defense against a newly characterized compression-boundary vulnerability ('relinking', a TOCTOU-style confused-deputy attack where prompt compression itself synthesizes a malicious instruction from benign fragments); reduces residual Backend Action Rate to 0.0-0.3% across configurations, substantially outperforming 11 existing defenses (input filters, sandwiching, SecAlign, CaMeL) on the security-utility Pareto frontier.
name: KBRA (Keyed Binding Reassembly Audit)

title: AgenticOS: An Intent-Oriented Secure Operating System Architecture for Autonomous AI Agents
defense_name: AgenticOS (Ghost Kernel / Logic Shutter / Agent Capsule / Semantic Boundary Gateway)
notes: Formally specified intent-oriented OS architecture explicitly reframing the OS as an 'intent filter' against prompt injection, malicious tool outputs, and capability-composition attacks; however the paper explicitly states there is no empirical implementation or evaluation, only qualitative architectural argument against five named threat classes.
name: AgenticOS (Ghost Kernel / Logic Shutter / Agent Capsule / Semantic Boundary Gateway)

title: PARSE: Provenance-Aware Retrieval Sanitization for Professional Domain LLM Agents
notes: Named domain-aware, fact-preserving sanitization pipeline targeting 'domain-camouflaged' indirect prompt injection that evades synthetic-benchmark-tuned defenses; rigorously evaluated with statistical significance testing against paraphrasing, spotlighting, sandwiching, and Llama Guard 3 on a real-enterprise-document benchmark, showing prior best synthetic-benchmark defense fails to generalize.
name: PARSE (Provenance-Aware Retrieval Sanitization)

title: Brain-Prompt Injection: A Route-Safety Audit for BCI-LLM Agents
notes: Formal audit-contract defense for a novel niche threat model (BCI-to-agent 'brain-prompt injection'); confirmation-plus-provenance routing empirically blocks the adaptive dual-decoder (C3) attack class to 0.000 rate versus 1.000 for agreement-plus-provenance alone, with formal proofs and conformal calibration, though the domain (EEG/BCI agents) is a narrow slice of the broader context-pollution literature.
name: Route-Safety Audit Contract (confirmation-plus-provenance routing)

title: SecureClaw: Clawing Back Control of LLM Agents
defense_name: SecureClaw (dual-boundary: effect-sink authorization + read-boundary plaintext confinement)
notes: Named dual-boundary architecture (handle-based plaintext confinement + PREVIEW-to-COMMIT effect authorization) with an explicit compromised-runtime threat model; rigorously evaluated in a common harness against IPIGuard, DRIFT, and Faramesh across AgentDojo, AgentLeak, and ASB, achieving 0% ASR on ASB and near-zero leak rates, with mechanism-isolation ablations proving both boundaries are non-substitutable.
name: SecureClaw (dual-boundary: effect-sink authorization + read-boundary plaintext confinement)

title: PRISM: Recovering Instruction Sets from Language Model Activations
notes: Named activation-to-language monitoring/detection technique recovering the full set of active instructions (including injected or covert ones) from hidden states via judge-guided GRPO training; substantially outperforms LatentQA, Activation Oracles, and text-only reporting baselines, with the largest gains specifically on adversarial-prompt-injection recovery.
name: PRISM (activation-conditioned instruction-set interpreter)

title: AgentSecBench: Measuring Prompt Injection, Privacy Leakage, and Tool-Use Integrity in LLM Agents
defense_name: AgentSecBench Combined defense stack (filtering + projection + redaction + delimiter annotation)
notes: Formal security-evaluation framework (three noninterference games) whose core contribution is a channel-closure measurement methodology rather than one single novel defense; however the evaluated Combined defense stack (composing four techniques) achieves 100% channel closure and 0.000 ASR/advantage across all games, the paper's own strongest proposed configuration.
name: AgentSecBench Combined defense stack (filtering + projection + redaction + delimiter annotation)

title: Device Context Protocol: A Compact, Safety-First Architecture for LLM-Driven Control of Constrained Devices
notes: Named protocol-layer defense (capability scoping, range/type checks, dry-run evaluation) for LLM-driven physical device control; rigorously evaluated against Raw MCP, IoT-MCP, and OpenAPI 3 baselines using AgentDojo's attack templates, rejecting 100% of capability-escalation and 78% of prompt-injection attempts versus 0-1% for MCP-family protocols.
